sources.title: JCGM 100:2008, Evaluation of Measurement Data — Guide to the Expression of Uncertainty in Measurement

contents.name: Clauses 2.2.3–2.3.6 and 3.1–3.2: measurand, standard uncertainty, Type A/B evaluation, corrections and reference-standard contributions
contents.reason: The definition preserves the input-model and correction conventions and distinguishes uncertainty evaluation method from random/systematic error type.

contents.name: Clauses 4.1.1–4.1.6: measurement function, input estimates and uncertainty distributions
contents.reason: The measurand, input estimates, correction/reference inputs and uncertainty-model distinction are stated explicitly.

contents.name: Clauses 5.1.2 and 5.2.1–5.2.5, Equations (10), (13) and (16): first-order sensitivity and covariance terms
contents.reason: The local proof establishes the exact variance of the linearized output and retains every off-diagonal covariance term; the GUM equation is treated as a first-order approximation for nonlinear output.

contents.name: Clauses 6.2 and 7.2: expanded uncertainty, confidence/coverage interpretation and reporting of combined standard uncertainty
contents.reason: The item states that combined standard uncertainty is not an interval and gives no coverage probability by itself.

sources.title: JCGM 100:2008/Amd.1:2026, Amendment 1: Nonlinearity in Measurement Models
sources.locator: Complete 5-page amendment; PDF p. 4 amends 4.1.4 and H.1.7 on significant nonlinearity and higher-order Taylor terms.

contents.name: Amended note to 4.1.4 and H.1.7: significant nonlinearity may require higher-order Taylor terms or another distribution-propagation treatment
contents.reason: Used only to bound the first-order approximation and identify when it may be inadequate.

contents.name: Monte Carlo treatment referenced by the amendment
contents.reason: The assigned design excludes Monte Carlo; no algorithm or claim about its implementation is included.

sources.title: NIST/SEMATECH Engineering Statistics Handbook, Chapter 2: Measurement Process Characterization

contents.name: Sections 2.3.1.2 and 2.3.2: reference standards and calibration as comparison with a reference base
contents.reason: Supports treating reference-standard values and their uncertainty as part of the declared calibration model.

contents.name: Sections 2.5.2–2.5.4: Type A and Type B uncertainty evaluation and the measurement-process context
contents.reason: The handbook explicitly classifies by evaluation method and discusses both random components and bias; the library definition keeps those categories distinct.

contents.name: Sections 2.3.6.4.1 and 2.3.6.7.1: day-specific calibration curves, future readings and covariance among calibration coefficients
contents.reason: The source's process example is observational evidence about one instrument, not a universal theorem; the library example uses its own stipulated two-batch curves.

contents.name: Sections 2.4.4.1, 2.4.5.3 and 2.4.6: repeatability, drift and representativeness of a gauge study
contents.reason: Supports keeping later-reading repeatability and process stability separate from calibration-curve uncertainty and treating adequacy empirically.

contents.name: Section 2.5.5: sensitivity coefficients and covariance in propagation-of-error calculations
contents.reason: Read as an independent applied treatment; the complete algebraic proof in the item comes from the local covariance supplier, not from the handbook's worked formula.

sources.retrieval_note: Browser opens of NIST's separate mpc54.htm, mpc56.htm and mpc57.htm pages returned HTTP 503. Their relevant content was recovered by inspecting the complete official Chapter 2 PDF at the cited source URL; no source or result was dropped.

sources.title: Sai Ravela, MIT OpenCourseWare, Quantifying Uncertainty: Summary lecture notes, Fall 2012
sources.locator: Complete 64-page course summary inspected at PDF pp. 16–17, headed ‘Uncertainty? Via Linearization’ and ‘Example: Double Pendulum’. The covariance update is propagated by the Jacobian of the model map.

contents.name: Uncertainty? Via Linearization, covariance propagation by the model Jacobian
contents.reason: This independent lecture-note treatment corroborates the first-order covariance-propagation context; the theorem's complete exact finite-dimensional variance proof is supplied locally.

contents.name: Double-pendulum covariance example following the linearization equations
contents.reason: The state-estimation example is not needed for the exact scalar calibration variance proof; the assigned worked example uses its own fully stipulated calibration inputs.

sources.title: JCGM 100:2008, Evaluation of Measurement Data — Guide to the Expression of Uncertainty in Measurement
sources.locator: Clauses 4.1 and 5.1–5.2, PDF pp. 20–35 / printed pp. 8–22: measurement function, input estimates, covariance and linearized combined standard uncertainty.

contents.name: Two-point calibration and covariance propagation used by the worked example
contents.reason: The example states a complete inverse calibration function and explicitly evaluates the shared-reference covariance contribution.

contents.reason: The worked numerical curves in this item are explicitly illustrative; the NIST example supports the process-drift caveat and is not treated as a universal law.
